name: How long does an open-concept kitchen conversion take in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How long does an open-concept kitchen conversion usually take in Los Angeles once permits and construction start?
mainEntity.text: How long does an open-concept kitchen conversion usually take in Los Angeles once permits and construction start?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timeline depends on scope. If the project is only widening an opening or removing a non-structural partition, construction may be fast. Once the job includes structural engineering, permit review, beam installation, electrical changes, flooring replacement, cabinetry, and finish work, the schedule expands significantly. In Los Angeles, the permit and plan-check phase can also affect the calendar before demolition begins. That is why two projects that look similar in photos can have very different durations. A realistic plan should separate preconstruction, permitting, demolition, structural framing, rough trades, inspections, drywall, finishes, and punch list time. Homeowners should also ask how long the kitchen will be unusable, since even a short project can be disruptive if the layout is fully opened and rebuilt at once. The best schedule is a written one with milestones, not a vague start-and-finish estimate.
acceptedAnswer.description: A simple wall-opening project can take a few days to a couple of weeks, but a full open-concept kitchen conversion with structural work, inspections, flooring, electrical, and finishes often takes several weeks to several months depending on scope and permit timing.
